newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Possible foreign listing news lifts Gencor.
newsitem.headline: Possible foreign listing news lifts Gencor.

text.p: News that South African mining house Gencor Ltd may be considering an offshore listing lifted its share price nearly two percent in fairly active trade on Monday, dealers said.
The group announced earlier it was considering accessing international markets to help fund future projects.
This followed close on the heels of weekend speculation that Gencor was planning to float a new mining group on the London Stock Exchange.
Monday's market was cheered by the news and the share jumped to 20 rand -- close to its year high of 20.50 rand -- from its previous close of 19.60 rand.
But by 0830 GMT Gencor had retreated a little to 19.90 rand with 198,900 shares changing hands.

Dealers said that the share was rising because Gencor's announcement was interpreted as meaning it planned the offshore listing of its Billiton offshore arm as a separate base metals company and Gencor Ltd as a precious metals company.

"Yes, it's definitely rising on the news of the separate listing of Billiton in London and a separate listing of Gencor, keeping it as a precious metals company. It's planning to separate the company along the lines of base metals and precious metals," said James Scott at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Britain's Observer newspaper said on Sunday that Gencor was planning to float a new mining operation in London which could be worth up to one billion pounds ($1.6 billion).

The paper said the new group would be built around mining subsidiary Billiton International and would also embrace large parts of Gencor's non-South African operations which mine gold, platinum, copper, zinc and tin.
"The news is being received positively. They've (Gencor) been looking for an offshore vehicle to expand their offshore operations," Scott said.
Gencor said earlier that it was evaluating major opportunities, including projects in South Africa, Mozambique, Venezuela, Brazil, Colombia and Australia.
It said its ability to compete for these projects would be significantly enhanced if it did not have to rely solely on its domestic capital market.
"Gencor is currently investigating a number of transactions that would provide its world-class asset base with such access to the international capital markets," it said.
The Observer said that the flotation was scheduled to take place before the end of the year.
